cases.question: Can I ship a production hotfix on a Thursday for a SEV2 incident, and how often must I post updates during that incident?
cases.answer:
Yes, with conditions. Production deploys normally can't go out on Thursdays, but the exception covers a hotfix for a SEV1 or SEV2 incident, so a SEV2 hotfix can ship on Thursday [deployment-process]. Every change still needs a pull request to `main` with one approving review and a green CI run [deployment-process]. Every production deploy also uses a canary: 10% of traffic for 15 minutes, then 100% if the error rate stays below 1% [deployment-process]. The documents describe the production deploy window as Sunday to Wednesday, 10:00 to 15:00 Riyadh time, but they don't say explicitly whether a hotfix is exempt from that window, so check with the VP of Engineering or the incident commander before deploying outside it. The runbook also prefers mitigation over diagnosis, so a rollback or feature-flag change may be a faster option than a new hotfix [incident-response-runbook]. A rollback uses the release pipeline with the previous tag and the rollback option, skips the canary, and takes about 5 minutes [deployment-process].

For updates, a SEV2 incident needs a post in the incident channel at least every hour, even if nothing has changed. Each update should say what we know, what we are trying, and when the next update will come [incident-response-runbook].
